items.titleEn: Gold price drops to $4,035/oz as Fed votes 10-2 in favor of rate hold
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – The Federal Reserve announced on Wednesday that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 in favor of maintaining the policy rate unchanged, as expected by the market consensus. “The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate,” the Federal Reserve said in its statement. “The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.” “Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace,” the statement read. “While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.”

South Korea fines Google and Apple over unfair app market practices
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: South Korea on Wednesday fined Alphabet's Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won ($47.6 million), saying they abused their dominance in app store markets by forcing local developers onto their own payment systems and by unfairly delaying app reviews. The Korea Media and Communications Commission, the country's media and telecommunications regulator, spent years investigating the U.S. tech giants for allegedly violating a 2021 law that prohibits app store operators from forcing developers to use specific payment systems.

Gold prices could fall to $3,900, silver to $50 as Fed tightening pressures precious metals – Sucden Financial
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices continue to hold critical support above $4,000 an ounce, but one investment firm expects prices to head lower by year-end as the Federal Reserve is expected to maintain its tightening bias, while silver faces even greater downside risks as weakening industrial demand adds to the pressure from elevated interest rates. In its latest quarterly metals report published Wednesday, analysts at Sucden Financial said they expect gold prices to test support around $3,900 an ounce ahead of the Federal Reserve's December monetary policy meeting. Meanwhile, silver prices could fall to between $50 and $53 an ounce as tighter monetary conditions continue to weigh on investment demand. Although the Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged Wednesday, markets see a nearly 80% chance of a rate hike in December.

U.S. copper stockpiling is squeezing China - Christopher Ecclestone
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) Washington’s strategic metals push is pulling copper into U.S. warehouses at China’s expense, according to Christopher Ecclestone, principal and mining strategist at Hallgarten + Company. Fresh from LME Week in London, Ecclestone told Kitco Mining’s Digging Deep on Oct. 22 that one metal dominated the conversations. “Copper, copper, copper,” he said. “This year it was massively, massively copper focused.” A chart from consultancy Project Blue captured the shift. “It showed that the Trump policies, for better or worse, are sucking copper into the US,” Ecclestone said. According to that chart, the U.S. ran a large inventory surplus last year and is heading for another, while China’s warehouse position has turned negative. “So the party that is suffering most, curiously enough, in the copper space is China, because the US is hoovering up material from all around the world.”
